title: Helping Your Pet Feel at Home in a Carrier
summary: Gentle, practical steps for making a carrier feel familiar before the first trip.
intro: A carrier is a new little space. Give your companion time to explore it at their own pace and build positive associations before you travel.
sections: Start at home
Place the carrier in a familiar room with the opening secured wide. Add a comfortable blanket and let your pet investigate without pressure.
Make it a happy place
Offer a favorite treat or toy near the entrance, then gradually inside. Let your pet choose when to approach and leave.
Practice in small steps
Once your pet is comfortable resting inside, try short periods with the door closed, then brief trips around the home.
Follow your pet's lead
Keep each session relaxed and short. If your pet seems stressed, pause and return to an easier step another day.
content: Let your pet explore the carrier at home, pair it with positive things, and build up to travel gradually.

title: A Simple Guide to Harness Fit
summary: How to measure your dog and check for a comfortable, secure harness fit.
intro: A well-fitting harness should feel secure and allow natural movement. A few careful measurements can help you find a good starting size.
sections: Measure the chest
Wrap a soft tape around the widest part of your dog's chest, just behind the front legs. Keep the tape snug without pulling tight.
Compare the size chart
Use the specific product's measurements rather than relying on weight or breed alone. Pets with similar weights can have different shapes.
Check movement
After adjusting the straps, check that your dog can walk, sit and turn comfortably. Look for rubbing or gaps and adjust as needed.
Recheck regularly
Fit can change with coat, age and weight. Inspect the adjustment points and hardware before outings.
content: Measure carefully, compare the product chart and check fit and movement before every walk.

title: Build a Little Pet Travel Kit
summary: A few useful essentials to keep close for a day out with your companion.
intro: A small, ready-to-go kit can make day trips smoother for both you and your pet. Start with the basics your companion already knows.
sections: Bring water and a bowl
Offer water regularly, especially on warm or active days. A collapsible bowl packs away easily after use.
Pack familiar comforts
A favorite treat, a small towel or a familiar blanket can help your pet settle in new places.
Keep cleanup supplies handy
Waste bags and a spare wipe are useful for quick stops and unexpected messes.
Check before you leave
Make sure harnesses, leads and carrier fastenings are in good condition and fit comfortably.
content: Pack water, familiar comforts and cleanup basics, then check the gear before heading out.
